activity_b.text: Good morning, please have a seat.
I’m Mr. Fernando, the training manager.
How are you today?
Good morning, sir. I’m doing well, thank you.
I’m a little nervous, but I can manage.
Don’t worry, this is a friendly interview.
So, Namal, I see that you finished school last year.
Can you tell me a bit about yourself?
Yes, sir. I completed my A’ level exam in August.
While I was still at SLGTI, I worked part-time at a small garage in Kandy.
I don’t have a lot of experience, but I can handle basic tasks confidently.
That’s good to hear.
What kind of work did you do there?
I helped the senior mechanic with repairing, oiling, and replacing vehicle parts.
Sometimes I assisted with more complex repairs.
I also spoke to customers when the garage was busy, finding out the problems that needed fixing in their vehicles.
I wasn’t responsible for big jobs, but I supported the team whenever they needed help.
Excellent.
What skills do you think you can bring to our company?
I can calibrate tools well, sir.
I know how to do wheel alignment carefully, and I started learning how to do some basic engineer repairs.
I also learnt how to stay calm when things get stressful.
I might need some guidance with adjusting the accelerator pedal, and replacing timing belt and fan belts at first, but I’m going to improve quickly.
That’s a good attitude.
How comfortable are you with radiator and fuel pump repairs?
I’m not an expert yet, but I can already do many basic repairs.
I might take more time with advanced and complex issues.
Excellent.
What are your plans for the next few years?
I’m going to complete this training programme and then try for an apprenticeship.
I might also follow additional short courses so I can expand my skills.
That sounds promising.
Thank you, Namal. We’ll contact you soon.
Thank you very much, sir. I appreciate the opportunity.
